_comment: Read by scripts/check_page_claims.py, proven by scripts/selftest_page_claims.py.
Two kinds of clause. `must_state` is something the page has to say, because
a reader who is not told it will get the next decision wrong. `must_not_state`
is something the page must never say, because it is not true of the product.
Patterns are SEMANTIC and deliberately narrow: they match the claim, not the
one sentence someone happened to write. A pattern is added here when a clause
of this shape appears, and the self-test's fixture corpus grows with it -- the
guard cannot become a rule with no evidence that it fires.

claims.because: Velero offers no client-side encryption for resource archives, so any Secret a backup captured is readable in the bucket. Plan 7.8 makes read access to a cluster's backups equivalent to cluster-admin on that cluster, and a page about that bucket that does not say so is the sentence an operator uses to hand out s3:GetObject.

An uncoordinated file-level copy of a running database copies its files at different moments, so it gives no consistency guarantee. Plan 7.5 lets the page describe the method and the hook annotations; it never lets a copy under neither be called consistent.

T4.8 and T4.9 record wall-clock times with their conditions -- data volume, host size, bandwidth -- and assert no recovery-time budget; section 10's rule is that a number without its conditions is not evidence. The page may quote the recorded runs; it may not turn one into a promise.
